title: Lifting an element modulo an ideal while avoiding finitely many primes that do not contain the ideal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an ideal I of a ring A and finitely many primes p_1, ..., p_r none of which contains I, every element of A/I lifts to an element of A avoiding all the p_i. The proof first removes inclusion relations among the primes, picks an arbitrary lift f, and lets S be the set of indices with f in p_s. If S is nonempty it forms the ideal J = I times the product of the p_i with i not in S, verifies that J is not contained in any p_s for s in S (using that there are no inclusions among the primes and that I is in none of them), invokes the avoidance lemma to find g in J outside all the p_s with s in S, and produces the solution f + g (proof lines 9069-9080). H2: the construction of the auxiliary ideal J and the avoidance step are the substance.
